[Spoiler=858 Case]Rain taps against the courthouse windows. Inside Courtroom 3A, cameras are banned from filming, but reporters are allowed to take part in reporting about the court cases. Two teens sit at the defense table. Rode Arlow, an anthropomorphic red fox. And Lizz Merry, an anthropomorphic Husky.
 
The courtroom doors open*

Two I.A.C. agents enter, Agent Mira Valen and Agent Darius Kelm.

The murmur quiets fills the courtroom*

Judge Halvern takes his seat.

Judge Halvern
 This court will now hear the case of the Commonwealth versus Arlow and Merry. Charges include conspiracy to aid a criminal syndicate, trafficking facilitation, and financial coordination.
The prosecutor rises*

Prosecutor Dane
 Your Honor, the evidence will show that these defendants knowingly assisted the 858 syndicate in distributing narcotics across three districts from New Westmore.
Lizz glances sideways at Rode*

Rode swallows*

The defense attorney stands slowly.

Defense Attorney Solen
 The evidence will show something else entirely that 858 targeted minors in vulnerable districts, manipulated their families through debt traps, and coerced participation under threat.
Agent Valen watches Rode carefully.

Agent Kelm folds his hands.

The prosecutor calls the first witness*

Agent Darius Kelm, Intelligence Agency of the Crime Department.

Kelm stands and walks to the front center of the courtroom*

Prosecutor Dane
 Agent Kelm, state your role for the court.

Agent Kelm
 I am a Field Operations Commander with the Intelligence Agency of the Crime Department. I oversee organized crime investigations tied to the 858 syndicate.

Prosecutor Dane
 Were you involved in the investigation of the defendants?

Kelm
 Yes. For fourteen months.

A murmur whispered in the back of the court* 

Prosecutor Dane
 What did your investigation uncover?

Prosecutor Dane
 Agent Kelm, did the defendants demonstrate awareness of the contents being transported?

Kelm 
Encrypted messages recovered from Rode Arlows device that include the phrase product secured and route clear. In the follow up exchanges, he asks about compensation rates tied to volume.

Defense Attorney Solen rises immediately*

Objection! Context omitted.

Judge Halvern
 Overruled for now. Continue.

Kelm finally glances at the teens*

Kelm 
However We also recovered communications showing threats issued to the Arlow household. Debt leverage was applied by the third party collectors affiliated with 858.

The courtroom shifts*

Defense Attorney Solen approaches slowly*

Agent Kelm, how old was Rode Arlow when recruitment began?

Kelm
 Sixteen.

And Lizz Merry?

Fifteen.

A heavier silence*

Is it standard 858 practice to recruit minors in these economically unstable districts?

Kelms jaw tightens*
Yes.

Does the I.A.C. have evidence of direct coercion?

Yes.

So while my clients transported materials, they did so under threat to their families?

Kelm hesitates*

Judge Halvern leans forward.
Evidence suggests coercive pressure was present.

The courtroom froze a bit. Prosecutor Dane scribbles notes quickly.

The prosecutor stands again*

Prosecutor Dane
Agent Kelm, regardless of coercion; did the defendants complete the exchanges knowingly?

Kelm answers carefully
Yes.

The word lands hard. And Judge Halvern calls a short recess, which gavel strikes in the courtroom.

Outside the courtroom doors, lots of reporters rushed to call in updates.

Inside, Rode leans forward, whispering to Lizz*

I didnt think theyd say it like that

Lizz exhales slowly*

Theyre not done yet.

A NCC Reporters 
We identified a recruitment pattern targeting minors in the eastern part of Neue Levbkurg City. The defendants were documented acting as couriers and following 858 orders. Surveillance footage places them at three confirmed exchange sites[/spoiler]
